articles.title: Litmus Music Secures $475 Million From Carlyle And KKR
articles.snippet:
Litmus Music has received approximately $475 million in new capital commitments from Carlyle and investment funds managed by KKR.
The post Litmus Music Secures $475 Million From Carlyle And KKR appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Litmus Music Secures $475 Million From Carlyle And KKR
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:10 AM
Litmus Music Secures $475 Million From Carlyle And KKR
Litmus Music has received approximately $475 million in new capital commitments from Carlyle and investment funds managed by KKR.
The financing will provide Litmus with additional flexibility to acquire music catalogs and related rights. Carlyle Global Credit, which helped establish Litmus alongside its management team in 2022, will retain a majority ownership position. KKR will join the business as a new strategic investor.
Expanding A $1.4 Billion Music-Rights Platform
Litmus manages approximately $1.4 billion in assets and has assembled a portfolio containing more than 100,000 copyrights and recordings.
The company’s portfolio includes music associated with artists and songwriters such as Katy Perry, benny blanco, Randy Newman, and Keith Urban. Litmus acquires and manages publishing rights and recorded-music rights across multiple genres, regions, and generations.
Carlyle initially supported the launch of Litmus with a $500 million commitment consisting of equity and debt. Its latest investment came through the firm’s Credit Opportunities strategy.
KKR is investing primarily through its Asset-Based Finance Partners II fund. Evercore served as financial advisor to Carlyle, while Latham & Watkins acted as Carlyle’s legal counsel. Kirkland & Ellis advised KKR.
KEY QUOTES:
“Together with Carlyle and our team, we’ve built Litmus into a scalable music rights management business rooted in trust, creativity, analysis and, above all, our passion for music. This investment marks an exciting next chapter for our company, providing meaningful additional capital to pursue new deals and accelerate growth.”
“We’re grateful for Carlyle’s continued partnership and look forward to working with our new strategic partner, KKR.”
Hank Forsyth, Co-Founder and CEO of Litmus Music
“At the heart of Litmus is our commitment to partnering with artists and songwriters and recognizing the enduring value of their work. With Carlyle’s continued support and KKR joining as a new investor, we’re excited to deepen those relationships, pursue new opportunities and bring more iconic music into the Litmus portfolio.”
Dan McCarroll, Co-Founder and Chief Creative Officer of Litmus Music

Crypto dealbook: November funding reaches $405.2 million as Variational leads the week
Crypto ventures have raised $405.2 million in November across 36 rounds. Variational led the latest week with a $110 million Series B.
By John Kim
Published Nov 23, 2026, 7:22 AM EST
Save Share
Mentioned assets
SOL Solana Data: CryptoRank · TokenPost
Crypto ventures have raised $405.2 million in November, with Variational accounting for the largest funding round of the week at $110 million. API, payments and artificial intelligence were the leading investment categories.
Crypto venture funding for November stands at $405.2 million.
A total of 36 funding rounds have been recorded for the month, raising $405.2 million.
Crypto ventures raised $1.85 billion across 52 rounds in October and $680.5 million across 53 rounds in September.
Variational recorded the largest round of the week, raising $110 million, or 49% of weekly funding.
November 16 Nomad ($30 million, Series C, Tether and others); Lart ($2.5 million, undisclosed stage, x21 Digital and others).
November 17 Codex ($30 million, Series A, Pantera Capital and others); Avenia (Prev. BRLA Digital) ($25 million, Extended Series A, Faction and others); TheHUB ($4 million, seed, Valor Capital Group and others); End Close ($3.5 million, seed, Foundation Capital and others); Stables (undisclosed amount, strategic, Tether); CoinGecko (undisclosed amount and stage, Solana Foundation).
November 18 Variational ($110 million, Series B, Bain Capital Crypto and others); Global MPC ($7.5 million, strategic, Paul Taylor and others); Null ($1.7 million, pre-seed, cyber Fund and others).
November 19 MetaComp ($10 million, Pre-Series A, Further Ventures and others); SCRYPT Digital (undisclosed amount, strategic, Tether).
The investment activity index fell 34% from the previous month over the latest 30-day period. Both the number of rounds and total funding declined.
There were 57 funding rounds during the period, down 13.64% from the previous month. Total investment fell 9.47% to $1.65 billion.
Average round sizes ranged from $3 million to $10 million, and strategic investments were the most active stage. API was the leading area of investment focus.
Over the past six months, API accounted for 29.13% of investment focus, followed by payments at 23.04%, artificial intelligence at 19.57%, real-world assets at 15.22% and developer tools at 13.04%.
The most active investors over the same period included YZi Labs (Prev. Binance Labs) with 28 investments, Coinbase Ventures with 26, Tether with 11, Circle and SBI Holdings with 10 each, MH Ventures with nine and Maven 11 Capital with eight.

articles.title: Draper Receives $315.7 Million For Trident II Guidance Engineering
articles.snippet:
The U.S. Navy has awarded Draper a $315.7 million contract modification for specialized engineering support related to the Trident II D5 Strategic Weapons System.
The post Draper Receives $315.7 Million For Trident II Guidance Engineering appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Draper Receives $315.7 Million For Trident II Guidance Engineering
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:36 AM
Draper Receives $315.7 Million For Trident II Guidance Engineering
The U.S. Navy has awarded Draper a $315.7 million contract modification for specialized engineering support related to the Trident II D5 Strategic Weapons System.
The cost-plus-fixed-fee modification adds work to contract N0003024C6001. It primarily covers engineering services associated with the missile system’s guidance subsystem, which supports navigation and accuracy throughout flight.
Strategic Weapons Engineering Support
Approximately 70% of the work will be performed in Cambridge, Massachusetts, while another 15% will take place in Pittsfield, Massachusetts.
The remaining work will be conducted in Buffalo, New York; Cape Canaveral, Florida; and El Segundo, California. Contract performance is expected to be completed by September 30, 2028.
The Navy will obligate the modification’s entire $315.7 million value at the time of the award using fiscal 2027 weapons-procurement funds. None of the obligated funding is scheduled to expire at the end of the current fiscal year.
The award was made on a sole-source basis. According to the Navy, the government determined that Draper was the only responsible source capable of meeting the requirement. The proposed contract action was previously published through the federal contracting portal.
The modification extends Draper’s engineering work on the Trident II D5 guidance system. The guidance subsystem is a mission-critical part of the strategic weapons platform, providing the navigation and control information required to maintain the missile’s intended flight path.
Portfolio Acquisition Executive Strategic Systems Programs, headquartered in Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

articles.title: Crowley Government Services Wins $270.4 Million Navy Vessel Operations Contract
articles.snippet:
Crowley Government Services has received a $270.4 million contract from the U.S. Navy's Military Sealift Command to operate and maintain six government-owned vessels supporting ocean surveillance and missile-range instrumentation missions. The firm-fixed-price contract includes pass-through elements and covers services performed at locations worldwide.
The post Crowley Government Services Wins $270.4 Million Navy Vessel Operations Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Crowley Government Services Wins $270.4 Million Navy Vessel Operations Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 8:54 PM
Crowley Government Services Wins $270.4 Million Navy Vessel Operations Contract
Crowley Government Services has received a $270.4 million contract from the U.S. Navy’s Military Sealift Command to operate and maintain six government-owned vessels supporting ocean surveillance and missile-range instrumentation missions. The firm-fixed-price contract includes pass-through elements and covers services performed at locations worldwide.
The award supports the continued operation of specialized vessels that provide important capabilities for U.S. naval surveillance, testing, and national defense activities.
Crowley Government Services will be responsible for operating and maintaining the vessels under the contract’s requirements, supporting their availability for assigned missions.
The contract includes an initial six-month performance period beginning December 1, 2026, with provisions allowing services to continue through May 2028 if the available extensions are exercised.
Six-Vessel Fleet
The contract covers five ocean-surveillance vessels and one missile-range instrumentation ship.
The ocean-surveillance vessels include USNS Victorious, USNS Able, USNS Effective, USNS Loyal, and USNS Impeccable.
The sixth vessel is USNS Howard O. Lorenzen, a missile-range instrumentation ship supporting specialized defense-related monitoring and measurement missions.
Ocean-surveillance vessels provide capabilities that support the Navy’s understanding of maritime activity and underwater operating environments.
These ships contribute to the broader surveillance infrastructure used to support naval operations and situational awareness.
Missile-range instrumentation vessels serve a different but complementary mission, providing specialized platforms for collecting data associated with missile testing and related defense activities.
Operating these vessels requires sustained maintenance, qualified maritime personnel, and coordination with Military Sealift Command to support operational requirements.
Through the contract, Crowley Government Services will provide operational and maintenance services intended to help keep the six vessels available for their assigned missions.
Contract Period And Extension Options
The initial firm period runs from December 1, 2026, through May 31, 2027.
The contract includes one six-month option that, if exercised, would extend performance through November 30, 2027.
A separate six-month extension available under federal acquisition regulations could further continue services through May 30, 2028.
These provisions give the Navy flexibility to maintain operational continuity while determining its longer-term requirements for the vessels.
The announced $270.4 million contract value reflects the overall award structure, including the described extension provisions.
However, compensation associated with optional performance periods depends on whether the government exercises those options.
The agreement will use fiscal 2027 Navy working-capital funding. The contract announcement did not specify the amount initially obligated at the time of award.
Sole-Source Procurement
Military Sealift Command awarded the contract without competition under a federal procurement exception allowing a sole-source award when only one responsible source can satisfy the government’s requirements.

articles.text:
Baltimore , Global , Washington DC
Commercial Real Estate , General Business
Prince George’s County Approves $215M Financing Plan for $1.4B Sphere at National Harbor
November 23, 2026
The proposed 6,000-seat entertainment venue advances as county officials seek new tax revenue, tourism growth and economic development.
The Sphere in Las Vegas
Prince George’s County has taken a major step toward bringing a $1.4 billion Sphere entertainment venue to National Harbor , with the County Council unanimously approving a $215 million financing package to support the development.
The proposed 6,000-seat venue, modeled after the high-tech Sphere in Las Vegas, would become a major new entertainment destination along the Potomac River, approximately 44 miles south of downtown Baltimore.
The financing approval follows months of negotiations over public investment, labor protections, local hiring and community benefits.
$215 Million Financing Package
Under the approved plan, Prince George’s County would issue $215 million in bonds backed by anticipated increases in tax revenues from the National Harbor area.
About $130 million of the proceeds would support construction of the Sphere, while the remaining financing would refinance existing debt.
The county would repay the tax increment financing bonds through designated revenues, including property taxes generated by increases in assessed property values.
Sphere Entertainment Co. has argued that public financing is necessary to make National Harbor competitive with other potential venue locations.
Economic Development and Tax Revenue
County Executive Aisha Braveboy has positioned the Sphere as an opportunity to diversify the county’s economy and offset anticipated revenue losses associated with the Washington Commanders’ planned departure and the closure of Six Flags.
Braveboy said the project could generate more than three times the tax revenue the county expects to lose from those developments.
Beyond ticket sales, the venue could stimulate additional spending at National Harbor hotels, restaurants, retail establishments and other businesses.
The development would also expand the region’s entertainment infrastructure, potentially attracting concerts, immersive productions, corporate events and visitors from across the Mid-Atlantic.
Local Business Participation and Employment
The financing agreement includes provisions designed to increase participation by Prince George’s County businesses and residents.
The project establishes several construction-related targets:
50% of eligible construction spending directed to county-based small businesses or locally owned and operated businesses.
40% of eligible construction spending targeted toward county-based minority businesses on a best-effort basis.
45% of eligible construction work hours targeted toward Prince George’s County residents on a best-effort basis.
Council members also agreed to communicate additional local business participation goals to the county executive.
Labor organizations welcomed provisions protecting hospitality and service workers’ ability to organize but expressed concerns about the absence of a formal Project Labor Agreement covering construction employment.
UNITE HERE Local 25, which represents hotel, restaurant and casino workers, supported labor peace provisions while criticizing the lack of stronger construction worker protections.
